name: xmedcon
why: Converting medical image formats like Analyze and DICOM is a real door into file formats, though the tool itself is fairly plumbing-like.

brief.what_it_is: XMedCon is an open-source toolkit for converting medical images between formats. The homepage's keyword list names ACR-NEMA, Analyze, DICOM, ECAT, GIF, Interfile, NIfTI and PNG among the formats it handles. The project ships three executables, medcon, xmedcon and xmedcon-config, and the SourceForge listing describes it as a command-line utility and library. The homepage does not spell out exactly which formats are input and which are output, so the writer should not assume every conversion direction is supported.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as a way to "lower at least one barrier in medical research projects" by making medical image data usable across the many incompatible formats used in the field. The author's publication frames it as an open-source answer to medical image conversion.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage and SourceForge listing do not describe the internal mechanism. The README was not reached, so the writer should not describe internals beyond the format list and the C implementation.
brief.install_notes: No install steps were seen on the homepage or SourceForge page. The SourceForge page lists Linux, Windows, Mac and BSD as operating systems, with a download button. Homebrew installs it as the xmedcon formula. Build or configuration steps were not seen, though the presence of an xmedcon-config executable suggests a build-config helper.
brief.standout: It is a long-lived, single-purpose converter that puts the old ACR-NEMA, Analyze, ECAT and Interfile formats next to NIfTI and DICOM in one tool. Its author published it in a nuclear medicine journal, which is an unusual origin for a format converter.
brief.status: Maintained, by the SourceForge evidence. The SourceForge page shows a last update of 2026-09-20 and 25 downloads this week, and the project was registered in 2000-10-22. The homepage is an old PmWiki page with no release notes, so this is not a strong signal. The page also has a stray line, 'Personal NixOS development environment with our hundliv color theme', which looks like a wiki-template artifact and is not about this project.
brief.caveats: The GIF and ECAT6 components carry non-GPL terms: GIF is (C) 1991 Alchemy Mindworks, Inc. and ECAT6 is (C) 1989-1993 CTI PET Systems, Inc. The homepage says the project is GPLv2-or-later (LGPL in places), with those exceptions. The homepage's own README pointer was not followed, so build pain and missing features could not be checked. The SourceForge reviews are sparse, with two reviews, both short.

a medical image conversion utility & library; hereby hoping to lower at least one barrier in medical research projects.
